content: Erythromycin is an antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It belongs to the macrolide class of antibiotics and is effective only against bacterial infections, not viral infections such as the common cold or flu. It may also be prescribed to prevent certain bacterial infections. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. Shake the bottle well before each dose and measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or spoon. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If you are using it to treat an infection, continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may result in a return of the infection. If you are taking it to prevent infections, follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain or cramping, and loss of appetite. Taking the medication with food may help reduce these symptoms. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, erythromycin may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Before taking erythromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other macrolide antibiotics (such as azithromycin or clarithromycin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Erythromycin may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase this risk, especially if you are using certain medications like diuretics or experiencing conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Erythromycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Some erythromycin products may contain sodium, which could be relevant for individuals on a sodium-restricted diet. Infants may be at higher risk for a serious stomach condition when taking this medication. Erythromycin passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of erythromycin from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Similarly, erythromycin can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, affecting how they work. This medication may also interfere with certain lab tests, such as urine tests, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Different brands of this medication may have different storage requirements. Check the product package for specific instructions or ask your pharmacist. Do not freeze the medication or store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
